title: The Cardinal Rule of Behavior Change
coreMove: Attach an immediate, sensory reward to a behavior whose real payoff is delayed, so the present self casts a vote the future self will thank it for.

exampleSpecs.domain: a pediatric ICU nurse trying to drink water across a twelve-hour shift after three years of chronic dehydration headaches
exampleSpecs.audience: a shift worker whose job punishes any pause
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she finishes the rotation without the 4pm migraine that has cost her two sick days a month
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she ties each finished water bottle to dropping a paperclip from one scrub pocket to the other, and notices that the small clink is what actually keeps her going, not the distant promise of feeling better

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance illustrator who keeps blowing through her quarterly tax set-aside
exampleSpecs.audience: a self-employed creative with irregular income
exampleSpecs.stakes: a $4,200 tax bill in April she has no plan to cover
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after each client payment hits, she must choose between the dopamine of an immediate purchase and a same-day transfer to a 'Future Me' account whose name and balance she sees every time she opens her banking app

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra teacher trying to give one specific piece of praise to every student each week
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher with 140 students across five sections
exampleSpecs.stakes: three of his seniors are quietly deciding whether to drop music next semester
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a week where he failed, he reconstructs why the gold-star sticker he gave himself on a desk calendar — not the abstract goal of 'being a better teacher' — was the satisfying signal that had been carrying the streak

exampleSpecs.domain: a recently widowed retiree trying to walk to the corner mailbox each morning after eight months of barely leaving the house
exampleSpecs.audience: a 71-year-old whose grief has hardened into immobility
exampleSpecs.stakes: her cardiologist's warning that another sedentary quarter will likely mean a second stent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places a single butterscotch candy on the kitchen counter to unwrap only on return, and the unwrapping — the foil, the smell — is what her body learns to walk toward, not the cardiologist's chart

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook studying for the food-handler recertification exam he has failed twice
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult learner with shaky reading confidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: losing the kitchen lead position he was promised if he passes by June
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: his sister, on a phone call, helps him design a thirty-minute study block that ends with him crossing off the day on a wall calendar in red marker, and they argue about whether the red mark is 'silly' until he admits the streak is the only reason he opened the book on Tuesday

exampleSpecs.domain: a city bus driver trying to stop snapping at his teenage daughter during the evening handoff
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent of a 14-year-old whose patience is gone by 5pm
exampleSpecs.stakes: a relationship that has gone from daily conversation to one-word answers in four months
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he writes one sentence in a pocket notebook each night naming a moment he stayed calm, and realizes the act of writing it — not the daughter's reaction, which is still cold — is the reward keeping the new response alive long enough for her to eventually notice
